sections.heading: Asking to be filled with you
sections.text: Holy Spirit, just as the sun is full of light, the sea is full of water, and heaven is full of glory, make my heart full of you. Do not let me live on the edges of your presence. Fill the empty places in me with your life, your holiness, your comfort, and your power.
theological_themes: The Holy Spirit personally indwells and fills believers.
The Christian life depends on the Spirit’s active presence, not merely on religious effort.
God’s fullness is abundant and life-giving.

scripture_references.connection: Paul commands believers to be filled with the Spirit, showing that the Christian life is meant to be lived under the Spirit’s ongoing influence and control.
This passage teaches that belonging to Christ includes the indwelling of the Spirit, whose presence gives life even to mortal people.

sections.heading: Needing you to make Christ real to me
sections.text: All the love the Father has planned, and all that Jesus has done to redeem me, must be made alive in me by your work. Open my eyes to see Jesus clearly. Make the unseen things of God more real to me than the loud and temporary things in front of me. Give me new life where I am dead, sight where I am blind, and faith where I cannot see.
theological_themes: The Spirit applies the saving work of Christ to believers.
The Spirit reveals Christ and enables spiritual understanding.

scripture_references.connection: Jesus teaches that entrance into God’s kingdom requires birth by the Spirit, grounding the prayer’s dependence on the Spirit for new life.
Jesus says the Spirit will guide his people into truth and glorify Christ, which directly supports the request to see Jesus clearly through the Spirit’s work.
Paul contrasts visible, temporary things with unseen, eternal realities, matching the prayer’s longing to perceive and live by the realities God reveals.

sections.heading: Confessing how empty and sluggish I am
sections.text: I confess that I am often cold toward you. I feel poor in spirit, empty, half-awake, and slow to serve. My prayers can be words without heart. My praise can be sound without wonder. I can look at glory and barely see it. Please do not let me grieve you, ignore you, or push back against your work in me.
theological_themes: Honest confession of spiritual coldness and weakness.
Believers can grieve or resist the Spirit’s work.
True worship and prayer require the Spirit’s life in the heart.

scripture_references.connection: Paul warns believers not to grieve the Holy Spirit, which supports the prayer’s concern about resisting or dulling the Spirit’s work.
Paul says the Spirit helps believers in their weakness, especially in prayer, which speaks to the confession of weak and inadequate praying.

sections.heading: Come and do your full work in me
sections.text:
Come with power, and drive out every sinful desire that still tries to rule me. Take the throne in my heart and keep me belonging to Christ.

Come as my teacher, and lead me into truth. Help me understand what I cannot grasp on my own.

Come as the love of God poured into me, so that I may adore the Father and love him as my greatest treasure.

Come as joy, living in me, stirring me, strengthening me, and making obedience more than duty.

Come as light, opening Scripture to me and shaping my life by what you show me there.

Come as the one who makes me holy. Let my body, soul, mind, desires, habits, and choices be yours.

Come as my helper. Strengthen me, guard me, and guide my steps today.

Come as the one who brings beauty out of disorder. Put what is confused in me back into your order. Make what is chaotic in me become Christlike and whole.
theological_themes: The Spirit empowers believers to put sin to death.
The Spirit teaches, guides, and illumines Scripture.
The Spirit pours God’s love into the heart and produces joy.
Sanctification involves the whole person being set apart for God.
The Spirit helps, strengthens, and directs believers in daily obedience.

scripture_references.connection: Paul says believers put sinful deeds to death by the Spirit and are led by the Spirit, grounding the prayer’s request for power over sin and daily direction.
Jesus identifies the Holy Spirit as the Helper who teaches and reminds his people of Christ’s words, supporting the prayer’s request for instruction and help.
Paul says God’s love is poured into believers’ hearts through the Holy Spirit, which directly supports the request to love and adore the Father by the Spirit’s work.
The psalmist asks God to open his eyes to behold his Word, fitting the prayer’s request for the Spirit to illuminate Scripture and shape obedience.
Paul prays for complete sanctification and grounds it in God’s faithfulness, supporting the prayer’s desire for the whole person to belong to God.

sections.heading: Make your glory visible in me
sections.text: Holy Spirit, show me more of your glory by making more of your life visible in me. Let your work in me honor you. Make my life carry the fragrance of Christ, so that what comes from me is not the stale smell of self, but the clean, living evidence that you are present.
theological_themes: The Spirit glorifies God by transforming believers.
Christian character is meant to display Christ.
The believer’s life can become a witness to the presence and work of God.

scripture_references.connection: Paul describes believers being transformed into the image of the Lord by the Spirit, which supports the prayer’s request that the Spirit be magnified through inward change.
Paul uses the image of the fragrance of the knowledge of Christ spreading through God’s people, fitting the prayer’s desire to carry the aroma of Christ in daily life.

content_provenance.original_author: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
content_provenance.original_source: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
content_provenance.source_copyright_status: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
content_provenance.modern_version_note: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

theological_issues_identified: The line about God’s purposes of love and Christ’s redemption being ‘vain’ without the Spirit’s inward work could sound as though God’s saving plan is objectively ineffective. I rendered it as the Spirit’s necessary application of salvation to the believer, not as any weakness in the Father’s purpose or Christ’s finished work.
The request for the Spirit ‘without measure’ was rendered as a plea for abundant fullness, not as a claim that a believer receives the Spirit in the unique way Christ does.
significant_interpretive_choices: I treated the prayer’s repeated ‘Come as...’ lines as descriptions of the Spirit’s many biblical works rather than as separate identities or modes of the Spirit.

I rendered ‘beautifier’ as the Spirit bringing Christlike order and wholeness out of inner confusion, because the original connects beauty with moral and spiritual restoration rather than mere outward attractiveness.
I interpreted the final ‘fragrance’ image as the believer carrying the aroma of Christ, drawing on Paul’s language in 2 Corinthians rather than making it a vague metaphor for personal influence.
